question:
(a) Explain the term resolving power of an optical instrument.
(b) For a telescope, explain how the aperture of the objective affects its resolving power.
(c) Why is a large aperture objective preferred in an astronomical telescope?

options.A:
(a) Resolving power is the ability to distinguish two nearby point objects separately.
(b) A larger objective aperture decreases the minimum angular separation that can be resolved and hence increases resolving power.
(c) A large aperture is preferred in an astronomical telescope because it collects more light for brighter images and improves resolution of close stars and fine details.
options.B:
(a) Resolving power is the magnifying power of an instrument.
(b) Increasing aperture decreases resolving power.
(c) A small aperture is preferred because it collects less light.
options.C:
(a) Resolving power is the ability to produce an upright image.
(b) Aperture affects only focal length, not resolution.
(c) A large aperture is preferred only to make the telescope shorter.
options.D:
(a) Resolving power is the brightness of an optical instrument.
(b) A larger aperture increases the minimum angular separation.
(c) A large aperture is preferred because it reduces magnification.
